sourceConsistency.situationalKeysAndAlternatives: All 5,095 active situational keys and 20,380 choice explanations checked by the evidence/answer-identity regression checks; source consistency is not independent clinical approval.

focusedSourceReview.scope: Read claim-specific passages for the 33 flagged sources or verified official replacements. Retained browser-readable guidance is distinguished from automated HTTP blocks.

duplicateScreening.method: TF-IDF cosine >= 0.35 on scenario/problem/action, and same exact keyed-answer tokens with stem-token Jaccard >= 0.65. Candidate flags require editorial adjudication. No guarantee is made about semantic overlap below thresholds.

newReplacement.reason: The prior ECT preparation case tested generic unresolved informed consent, already covered by the five-part general surgical-consent case. The replacement tests relapse-prevention planning after an acute ECT response, retaining four active seven-part cases for this topic.
newReplacement.sourceClaim: Medication and follow-up support commonly continue after an acute ECT course; continuation or maintenance ECT may help selected people avoid relapse. No fixed schedule is prescribed in the reviewer case.

retainedScenarioPairs.reason: Postpartum endometritis differs from intrapartum intraamniotic infection and fetal tachycardia.
CPP subtracts ICP from MAP; the second question calculates MAP from systolic and diastolic pressure. Equal numerical results do not make the quantities interchangeable.
Classifying a calm toddler against an age-specific respiratory threshold differs from obtaining a reliable rate in a crying child.
A normal thrill in a functioning fistula differs from a newly absent thrill requiring access-patency assessment.
Dengue warning signs and maternal pregnancy danger signs occur in different clinical contexts and require different focused follow-up.
Respiratory acidosis from raised carbon dioxide differs from a combined respiratory and metabolic disturbance.
Diarrheal bicarbonate loss causes metabolic acidosis; gastric suction causes metabolic alkalosis. The keys represent opposite disturbances.
Diarrheal metabolic acidosis differs from combined respiratory and metabolic acidosis with separate respiratory impairment.
Renal hypoperfusion after general fluid loss differs from measured high-output ileostomy losses and stoma-specific monitoring and replacement.
Infection-associated shock differs from hemorrhagic shock and requires different cause-directed treatment in addition to support.
A kinked catheter causing postrenal obstruction and possible AKI differs from the same trigger causing autonomic dysreflexia in a susceptible spinal-cord injury.
A potassium-replacement safety problem differs from acute symptomatic tachyarrhythmia management.
A child with a febrile seizure differs from an adult generalized seizure; cause and age-specific evaluation differ despite shared seizure precautions.
Chemotherapy vesicant extravasation differs from norepinephrine extravasation in a person who still needs circulatory support. Drug-specific management and alternative access differ.
An unclear procedural-consent discussion differs from a specific language barrier requiring a qualified interpreter.
Suspected uterine rupture differs from intraamniotic infection and has different immediate obstetric implications.
Respiratory carbon-dioxide retention differs from metabolic bicarbonate loss, with different ABG patterns and causes.
Confirmed ventricular fibrillation needing defibrillation differs from a flat tracing with a detached electrode, requiring immediate patient and equipment assessment.
A direct hopeless/self-harm statement differs from increased energy while hopelessness persists during treatment; the timing changes suicide-risk assessment.
Unsafe potassium replacement differs from potassium falling during insulin treatment of DKA; the latter requires coordinated insulin, potassium and metabolic review.
A kinked chest drainage tube causing thoracic compromise differs from a kinked urinary catheter triggering autonomic dysreflexia.

preservation.allowedChanges: 167 reviewed URL fields on 71 records; retirement flags on seven ECT consent questions. Seven new ECT relapse-prevention records use fresh IDs. Restoring only those changes reproduces the full previous content digest. Existing stems, choice order, answer positions and explanations are unchanged.

limits: Full-bank structural, answer-identity and reference-fact consistency checks plus focused primary-source clinical review and similarity adjudication. This is not an independent nursing educator review of every clinical claim and cannot guarantee zero errors.
